definitions.explanation: An endearing honorific suffix used mainly for children and young women.

examples.japanese: {花子|はなこ}ちゃん、⟦こんにちは→こんにちは：02839_konnichiha⟧。
⟦お{婆|ばあ}ちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{家|いえ}→家：00612_ie⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧。
⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{泣|な}いている→泣く：00655_naku⟧。

notes:
〜ちゃん is an affectionate honorific suffix expressing closeness and endearment.

WHO IT'S USED FOR:
- Children, especially girls
- Close female friends (among women)
- Babies and toddlers
- Family members (informal)
- Pets
- Sometimes used by/for boys in early childhood

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦お{母|かあ}ちゃん→お母ちゃん：21588_okaachan⟧: mommy (informal)
- ⟦お{婆|ばあ}ちゃん→おばあちゃん：10968_obaachan⟧: grandma
- ⟦お{爺|じい}ちゃん→おじいちゃん：20642_ojiichan⟧: grandpa
- ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧: baby (standard, not just affectionate)

HONORIFIC HIERARCHY (informal → formal):
- 〜ちゃん: affectionate, intimate
- 〜⟦{君|くん}→君：01998_kun⟧: familiar (mainly for boys/male juniors)
- 〜⟦さん→さん：09848_san⟧: polite, general-purpose
- 〜⟦{様|さま}→様：01549_sama⟧: very formal, respectful

Using 〜ちゃん with someone you're not close to can seem overly familiar or condescending. In workplace settings, it is generally inappropriate except among very close colleagues.
